questions.question: If a trailer starts to jackknife, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Let the wheels grip the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: When a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the wheels regain grip with the road. Do not use the trailer hand brake because it will make the skid worse. Braking is what caused the wheels to lock up in the first place.

questions.question: Changing lanes quickly can cause:

options.text: A whip effect that may cause a rollover.
Other drivers to be confused about which lane you will use.

questions.correctAnswerText: A whip effect that may cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: Changing lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle can create a whip effect that may cause a rollover.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: A combination vehicle has two air lines: one for service brakes and one for emergency brakes.

questions.question: A lightly loaded combination vehicle stops more slowly than a fully loaded one because:

options.text: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give high traction.
Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give low traction.
Brakes only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.
Suspension springs only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give low traction.
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle takes longer to stop than a fully loaded one. Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have less traction on a light trailer than on a heavy one.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: Requires more skill
questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle requires more skill than driving a single vehicle because combination vehicles are longer and heavier.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible inside the trailer.
Placed as low as possible inside the trailer.
Placed on the passenger side of the trailer.
Placed on the driver's side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible inside the trailer.
questions.explanation: Keep cargo weight as low to the ground as possible to reduce rollover risk. Do not place weight on just one side of the trailer because it could tilt and cause a rollover.

questions.question: Trailers with low clearance underneath are hard to drive:
questions.correctAnswerText: Over railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Low-clearance trailers are difficult to drive over railroad crossings, especially low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers.

questions.question: If cargo is loaded on only one side of a trailer, the trailer:

options.text: May get extra support when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May lean and could rollover.
questions.explanation: Loading cargo on one side of a trailer causes it to lean, which increases rollover risk.

questions.question: When lightly loaded, combination vehicles:

options.text: Should have most weight in the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have reduced braking ability.
questions.explanation: Lightly loaded combination vehicles have poor traction. Wheels lock up easily when stopping a light vehicle.

questions.question: A tractor protection valve is:

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that helps the battery recharge.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: What happens if you do not keep the fifth wheel plate properly greased?
questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause steering problems.
questions.explanation: A fifth wheel plate that is not properly greased creates friction between the tractor and trailer. This friction can cause steering problems.

questions.question: What happens when a combination vehicle turns a corner?

options.text: Make the turn as tight as possible.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
The rear wheels should go over the curb.
It is okay to knock over street signs if they are too close to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: When turning a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. Trailers make this effect more noticeable.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?
questions.correctAnswerText: An eight-sided red knob
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control is an eight-sided red knob on newer vehicles. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: What is a bobtail?

options.text: A tractor that drives faster than the speed limit
A tractor that drives slower than the speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: A tractor without a trailer
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor with no trailer attached. Drivers must be careful when operating a bobtail tractor.

questions.question: How should you load cargo to reduce the risk of a rollover?

options.text: Load the cargo as far forward as possible.
Load the cargo as far back as possible.
Load the cargo as low as possible.
Stack the cargo as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load the cargo as low as possible.
questions.explanation: To reduce the risk of a rollover, keep cargo as close to the ground as possible. Also, take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: What happens when the wheels of a trailer lock up?

options.text: The trailer will swing to one side.
The cab will swing, but the trailer stays straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will swing to one side.
questions.explanation: When trailer wheels lock up, the trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is especially likely if the trailer is not heavily loaded.

questions.question: How do fully-loaded rigs compare to empty rigs when it comes to rolling over?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over.
They are more likely to roll over.
They are equally likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity due to the cargo weight. This makes them 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn the top of the wheel in the direction you want the trailer to go.
Turn the top of the wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
It depends on where you are backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the top of the wheel away from where you want to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, switch the wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What does the emergency air line do?

options.text: It is controlled by the foot brake.
It is connected to the relay valves.
It supplies air to the trailer air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and it controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: After coupling, how much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.correctAnswerText: No space
questions.explanation: Before driving, inspect all couplings carefully. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
